answer: Quadratic staking locks collateral proportional to the square of each validator's bond, turning the protocol's capital inlet into a super-linear liquidity sink. Any attempt to forge a Sybil cluster commits O(n^2) stake for n identities, so marginal attack cost grows as Theta(k^2) while extractable value rises linearly, yielding negative expected utility. When aggregate stake exceeds the sable security threshold, slashing and verifiable-delay penalties enforce a Nash equilibrium where no rational adversary can profitably deviate.
